questions.question: 次の＿交差＿点を右に曲がりましょう。

opts: ごうざ – không có từ này
ごうさ – không có từ này
✔ こうさ – 交差, giao nhau (GIAO SAI)
こうざ – 口座 'tài khoản', chữ khác
ex.trans: Chúng ta hãy rẽ phải ở ngã tư tiếp theo.
ex.note: 交差点 こうさてん = ngã tư. 差 đọc さ (âm trong); 口座 こうざ là tài khoản ngân hàng.

questions.question: いただいたお菓子を＿早速＿食べました。

opts: さそく – không có từ này (thiếu っ)
✔ さっそく – 早速, ngay lập tức (TẢO TỐC)
さそっく – không có từ này
さっそうく – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tôi đã ăn ngay số bánh kẹo được tặng.
ex.note: 早速 = TẢO TỐC, đọc さっそく: làm ngay việc vừa nhận/được nghe.

questions.question: 日曜日は＿つごう＿が悪いので他の日にしてもらえませんか。

opts: ✔ 都合 – つごう, sự thuận tiện, hoàn cảnh (ĐÔ HỢP)
相当 – そうとう, tương đương, khá
予定 – よてい, dự định
具合 – ぐあい, tình trạng (sức khỏe, máy)
ex.trans: Chủ nhật tôi không tiện, đổi sang ngày khác được không?
ex.note: 都合が悪い = không tiện (về thời gian, hoàn cảnh). 都 đọc つ trong từ này.

questions.question: 世界の＿けいざい＿はだんだんよくなっています。

opts: 經済 – chữ phồn thể 經, không dùng trong tiếng Nhật hiện đại
✔ 経済 – けいざい, kinh tế (KINH TẾ)
經緕 – sai cả hai chữ
経緕 – 緕 không phải chữ đúng
ex.trans: Kinh tế thế giới đang dần tốt lên.
ex.note: Tiếng Nhật dùng chữ giản thể 経 (không phải 經); 済 bộ Thủy, không phải bộ Mịch 糸.

questions.question: 日本らしいお＿みやげ＿を発表されました。

opts: 進物 – しんもつ, đồ biếu tặng
贈物 – おくりもの, quà tặng
✔ 土産 – みやげ, quà mang về từ chuyến đi (THỔ SẢN)
産物 – さんぶつ, sản vật
ex.trans: Họ đã công bố những món quà lưu niệm mang đậm chất Nhật Bản.
ex.note: お土産 みやげ là cách đọc đặc biệt (熟字訓), không đọc theo từng chữ.

questions.question: ＿けいご＿の使い方はむずかしいです。

opts: 啓話 – không có từ này
啓語 – không có từ này (啓 KHẢI)
敬話 – không có từ này
✔ 敬語 – けいご, kính ngữ (KÍNH NGỮ)
ex.trans: Cách dùng kính ngữ rất khó.
ex.note: 敬 (KÍNH, tôn kính) khác 啓 (KHẢI, mở ra, 拝啓). 語 = ngôn ngữ, 話 = câu chuyện.

questions.question: このスーパーでは主にゆにゅう品を＿はんばい＿しています。

opts: 乱売 – らんばい, bán phá giá (ít dùng)
✔ 販売 – はんばい, bán hàng (PHIẾN MẠI)
特売 – とくばい, bán hạ giá
即売 – そくばい, bán tại chỗ
ex.trans: Siêu thị này chủ yếu bán hàng nhập khẩu.
ex.note: Chỉ 販売 đọc はんばい; 販 (PHIẾN) có bộ Bối 貝 liên quan đến tiền bạc.

questions.question: そんなにおこらないで＿れいせい＿になってください。

opts: 怜静 – 怜 sai chữ
怜靜 – sai cả hai chữ
冷靜 – 靜 là chữ phồn thể, không dùng
✔ 冷静 – れいせい, bình tĩnh (LÃNH TĨNH)
ex.trans: Đừng giận dữ như vậy, hãy bình tĩnh lại.
ex.note: 冷 bộ Băng 冫 (lạnh), khác 怜 bộ Tâm. 静 là chữ giản thể dùng ở Nhật.

questions.question: 毎日練習したのでテニスが（　）しました。

opts: 上手 – giỏi (tính từ); không đi với する
✔ 上達 – tiến bộ; luyện mỗi ngày nên tiến bộ
得意 – sở trường; không đi với しました ở đây
上等 – hảo hạng (đồ vật); không hợp
ex.trans: Nhờ luyện tập mỗi ngày mà tennis của tôi đã tiến bộ.
ex.note: 〜が上達する = kỹ năng tiến bộ. 上手 là tính từ な, phải nói 上手になる.

questions.question: （　）がないので何も食べたくありません。

opts: 食品 – thực phẩm; không hợp
食物 – đồ ăn; không hợp
✔ 食欲 – cảm giác thèm ăn; không thèm ăn
食事 – bữa ăn; 'không có bữa ăn' trái logic câu
ex.trans: Tôi không thấy thèm ăn nên chẳng muốn ăn gì.
ex.note: 食欲がない = chán ăn, không muốn ăn; 欲 = DỤC (ham muốn).

questions.question: どんなに大変な状態になっても（　）は失わないでください。

opts: 願望 – mong ước; không đi với 失う
有望 – có triển vọng (tính từ); không hợp
絶望 – tuyệt vọng; ngược ý
✔ 希望 – hy vọng; đừng đánh mất hy vọng
ex.trans: Dù rơi vào hoàn cảnh khó khăn đến đâu cũng đừng đánh mất hy vọng.
ex.note: 希望を失う = mất hy vọng, 希望を持つ = có hy vọng.

questions.question: 外交（　）になって海外で仕事がしたいです。

opts: ✔ 官 – quan chức; 外交官 = nhà ngoại giao
者 – 外交者 không có
員 – 外交員 là nhân viên bán hàng lưu động, không phải ngoại giao
人 – 外交人 không có
ex.trans: Tôi muốn trở thành nhà ngoại giao và làm việc ở nước ngoài.
ex.note: 〜官 = viên chức nhà nước: 外交官, 警察官.

questions.question: メイさんは（　）がいいのでみんなに好かれています。

opts: 精神 – tinh thần; không hợp với 'được yêu mến'
人物 – nhân vật; không đi với がいい
行動 – hành động; không tự nhiên
✔ 性格 – tính cách; tính tốt nên được mọi người quý
ex.trans: Mei có tính cách tốt nên được mọi người yêu quý.
ex.note: 性格がいい = tính tốt; 性格が明るい = tính vui vẻ.

questions.question: ワンさんの息子さんは（　）医者になりたいそうです。

opts: 未来 – tương lai (xa, chung); không dùng cho ước mơ cá nhân
✔ 将来 – tương lai (của một người); sau này muốn làm bác sĩ
前途 – tiền đồ; không dùng như phó từ
以後 – từ sau đó; không hợp
ex.trans: Nghe nói con trai anh Wang sau này muốn làm bác sĩ.
ex.note: 将来 = tương lai của bản thân (将来の夢); 未来 = tương lai xa, của nhân loại.

questions.question: 新入生飲迎会の（　）は終わりましたか。

opts: ✔ 準備 – chuẩn bị; chuẩn bị tiệc xong chưa
整理 – sắp xếp; không hợp với buổi tiệc
会場 – hội trường; không đi với 終わる
用心 – cẩn thận; không hợp
ex.trans: Việc chuẩn bị tiệc chào đón tân sinh viên đã xong chưa?
ex.note: 準備が終わる/できる = chuẩn bị xong. (飲迎会 trong đề là lỗi gõ của 歓迎会.)

questions.question: 明日駅前に8時に（　）してください。

opts: 集配 – thu gom và phân phát (bưu kiện); không hợp
集中 – tập trung (tinh thần); không hợp với địa điểm
✔ 集合 – tập hợp; tập trung ở trước ga lúc 8 giờ
収集 – thu thập (đồ vật, rác); không dùng cho người
ex.trans: Ngày mai hãy tập trung ở trước ga lúc 8 giờ.
ex.note: 集合する = nhiều người tụ họp tại một chỗ theo hẹn; 集合時間 = giờ tập trung.

questions.question: ピザをもらいたいとき（　 　 ) に行かなければならない。

opts: 市役所 – tòa thị chính; không cấp visa
郵便局 – bưu điện; không hợp
県庁 – trụ sở tỉnh; không hợp
✔ 大使館 – đại sứ quán; nơi xin visa
ex.trans: Khi muốn xin visa thì phải đến đại sứ quán.
ex.note: ピザ trong đề là lỗi gõ của ビザ (visa); ビザを申請する ở 大使館.

questions.question: 医者が母の病気をガンと（　）しました。

opts: 定義 – định nghĩa; không hợp
判別 – phân biệt, nhận dạng; không phải từ y khoa
決定 – quyết định; bác sĩ không 'quyết định' bệnh
✔ 診断 – chẩn đoán; bác sĩ chẩn đoán là ung thư
ex.trans: Bác sĩ đã chẩn đoán bệnh của mẹ tôi là ung thư.
ex.note: AをBと診断する = chẩn đoán A là B; 健康診断 = khám sức khỏe.

questions.question: 車が壊れたので（　）しなければなりません。

opts: 改善 – cải thiện (tình trạng); không dùng cho xe hỏng
改良 – cải tiến (sản phẩm); không hợp
✔ 修理 – sửa chữa; xe hỏng thì phải sửa
修正 – chỉnh sửa (văn bản, lỗi); không dùng cho máy
ex.trans: Xe bị hỏng nên phải sửa.
ex.note: 修理 = sửa máy móc, đồ vật; 修正 = sửa lỗi, sửa nội dung (文章を修正する).

questions.question: 今年に入って急に食料品の＿値段＿が高くなった。

opts: 価値 – giá trị
物価 – vật giá (mức giá chung)
✔ 価格 – giá bán; đồng nghĩa 値段
原価 – giá gốc
ex.trans: Từ đầu năm nay, giá thực phẩm đột nhiên tăng cao.
ex.note: 値段 ねだん = giá của một món hàng = 価格 かかく (cách nói trang trọng hơn).

questions.question: 3 年かかった工事がやっと＿完了＿しました。

opts: 投了 – chịu thua (cờ)
満了 – mãn hạn (hợp đồng)
修了 – hoàn thành khóa học
✔ 終了 – kết thúc; gần nghĩa nhất với 完了
ex.trans: Công trình kéo dài 3 năm cuối cùng đã hoàn tất.
ex.note: 完了 (HOÀN LIỄU) = hoàn tất trọn vẹn; 修了 chỉ dùng cho khóa học, 満了 cho thời hạn.

questions.question: 父は毎日会社で＿一生懸命＿働いています。

opts: ✔ 熱心に – nhiệt tình, chăm chỉ; đồng nghĩa 一生懸命
熱中に – sai dạng (phải là 熱中して)
本気で – nghiêm túc, thật lòng
夢中で – say mê quên hết
ex.trans: Bố tôi ngày nào cũng làm việc chăm chỉ ở công ty.
ex.note: 一生懸命 = hết sức, cố gắng hết mình ≈ 熱心に (nhiệt tâm, chăm chỉ).

questions.question: あの人きょろきょろして＿様子＿が変ですよ。

opts: 表情 – nét mặt
事情 – hoàn cảnh, lý do
✔ 態度 – thái độ, cử chỉ; gần nghĩa 様子 ở đây
服装 – trang phục
ex.trans: Người kia cứ nhìn ngó lung tung, cử chỉ lạ lắm.
ex.note: 様子 = dáng vẻ, tình trạng bên ngoài; ở đây chỉ cách hành xử, nên gần với 態度. きょろきょろ = nhìn ngó xung quanh.

questions.question: この書類に必要事項を＿記入して＿提出してください。

opts: 上書きして – ghi đè
✔ 書き入れて – điền vào; đồng nghĩa 記入して
書き取って – chép lại (nghe rồi viết)
清書して – chép sạch lại
ex.trans: Hãy điền các mục cần thiết vào giấy tờ này rồi nộp.
ex.note: 記入する (KÝ NHẬP) = điền thông tin vào mẫu đơn.

questions.question: 成長
options: 本が＿成長＿で屋根まで届いています。
親の仕事は＿成長な＿子どもです。
苦しい生活が私の＿成長＿を早めました。
彼は＿成長＿がいい子どもです。
questions.explanation:
1 sai vì nên dùng "成長して".
2 sai vì không dùng "成長+danh từ"
3 đúng vì miêu tả sự trưởng thành của người và động, thực vật.
4 sai không dùng cách nói "成長がいい" nên dùng là "早い／遅(い”

opts: Sai: sách chất cao nên dùng 積み上がって
Sai: 成長 không đi kiểu 成長な; nên dùng 子どもの成長
✔ Đúng: cuộc sống khó khăn khiến tôi trưởng thành sớm
Sai: ý 'phát triển tốt' nên dùng 発育がいい
ex.trans: Cuộc sống vất vả đã khiến tôi trưởng thành sớm hơn.
ex.note: 成長 = sự lớn lên, trưởng thành (người, cây, kinh tế); là danh từ/động từ する, không có dạng 成長な.

questions.question: もえる
options: おいしく＿もえた＿魚を食べましょう。
ゴミ庭で＿もえて＿ください。
このクラスには心が＿もえる＿ひとが多いです。
＿もえる＿ような恋がしてみたいです。
questions.explanation:
1 sai vì "もえた魚" không ăn được.
2 sai vì tha động từ cần nói là "もやしてください"
3 sai vì không nói "心がもえるひと" mà phải sử dụng "もえる（ような）心を持っている人"
4 đúng vì もえるような恋 diễn tả tình cảm mãnh liệt.

opts: Sai: cá nướng là 焼けた
Sai: đốt rác (tha động từ) là もやして; ゴミ庭 là lỗi gõ
Sai: nên nói 燃えるような心を持つ人
✔ Đúng: muốn yêu một cuộc tình cháy bỏng
ex.trans: Tôi muốn thử một lần yêu say đắm cháy bỏng.
ex.note: 燃える もえる = cháy (tự động từ); nghĩa bóng: bừng cháy cảm xúc. Tha động từ là 燃やす.

questions.question: 家庭
options: 彼女はお父さんとお母さんの3人＿家庭＿です。
彼女は大変貧しい＿家庭＿で育ちました。
彼女の＿家庭＿は3階段でとても広いです。
＿家庭＿がなかが悪いので彼女は早く家を出たがっていました。
questions.explanation:
1 sai vì nên nói là "家族"
2 đúng vì diến tả nơi mà gia đình sinh sống.
3 sai vì nên sử dụng "家"
4 sai vì nên sử dụng "家族"

opts: Sai: ba người gồm bố mẹ là 家族
✔ Đúng: lớn lên trong gia đình nghèo
Sai: căn nhà 3 tầng là 家
Sai: các thành viên không hợp nhau là 家族
ex.trans: Cô ấy lớn lên trong một gia đình rất nghèo.
ex.note: 家庭 = gia đình như một tổ ấm, môi trường sống; 家族 = các thành viên; 家 = ngôi nhà.

questions.question: かくす
options: 向こうから意地悪な人が来たので母の後ろに＿かくして＿しまいました。
使ったおもちゃはきちんと箱に＿かくして＿おきなさい。
父があまりたばこを吸うので＿かくして＿しまいました。
あなたから＿かくさない＿話をくわしく聞かなければなりません。
questions.explanation:
1 sai vì cần sử dụng tự động từ "かくれて"
2 sai vì cần sử dụng "しまって”　(thu nhập)
3 đúng vì sử dụng với nghĩa là cất giấu để người khác không tìm thấy.
4 sai vì nên dùng "本当の話"

opts: Sai: tự trốn là かくれて
Sai: cất đồ chơi vào hộp là しまって
✔ Đúng: bố hút thuốc nhiều nên giấu thuốc đi
Sai: ý 'không giấu giếm' nên dùng かくさずに話す
ex.trans: Bố hút thuốc nhiều quá nên tôi đã giấu (thuốc) đi.
ex.note: 隠す かくす = giấu (tha động từ); 隠れる かくれる = trốn (tự động từ).

questions.question: 現実
options: 好きなことだけしていたいけど、理想と＿現実＿は違います。
宇宙に行くことが＿現実＿にするは100年前には思わなかっただろう。
今日＿現実＿で100人が講習の参加を申し込んでいます。
長い間のゆめだった老人ホームの建設の＿現実＿ができました。
questions.explanation:
1 đúng vì diễn tả sự việc hoặc trạng thái thực diễn ra trước mắt.
2 sai vì nên dùng "なる”　thay cho "する" và dùng "を”　thay cho "が”
3 sai vì nên dùng "現在で”
4 sai vì phải dùng "建設が現実になった、実現した".

opts: ✔ Đúng: lý tưởng và hiện thực khác nhau
Sai: phải nói 現実になる (trở thành hiện thực)
Sai: thời điểm hiện tại là 現在
Sai: ước mơ thành sự thật là 実現
ex.trans: Tôi chỉ muốn làm điều mình thích, nhưng lý tưởng và hiện thực thì khác nhau.
ex.note: 現実 = hiện thực (↔ 理想 lý tưởng). Đừng nhầm với 実現 = biến thành hiện thực.

questions.exam: tryjlpt 2014年12月 日本語能力試験 N3
questions.question: 今度の旅行は、交通費が5,000円で、ホテルが10000円なので、_____ 15,000円かかります。

opts: 共通 – chung; không hợp
全体 – toàn thể; không dùng cho tính tổng tiền
集中 – tập trung; không hợp
ex.trans: Chuyến đi lần này phí đi lại 5.000 yên, khách sạn 10.000 yên nên tổng cộng hết 15.000 yên.
ex.note: 合計 (HỢP KẾ) = tổng cộng các khoản; đứng trước số tiền như phó từ.

questions.exam: tryjlpt 2014年12月 日本語能力試験 N3
questions.question: 縮小
options: ここは病院ですから、もう少し声を＿縮小＿してください。
作文を何度も書き直していたら消しゴムが＿縮小＿してしまいました。
この写真はちょっと大きいので、コピーするときに少し＿縮小＿してくださ。
そのゲームでは何度も遊んだので、もう興味が＿縮小＿しました。

opts: Sai: nói nhỏ lại là 小さく
Sai: tẩy mòn đi là 小さくなって
✔ Đúng: thu nhỏ ảnh khi photo
Sai: hết hứng thú là なくなりました
ex.trans: Bức ảnh này hơi to nên khi photo hãy thu nhỏ lại một chút.
ex.note: 縮小 (SÚC TIỂU) = thu nhỏ quy mô, kích thước (↔ 拡大 phóng to): 縮小コピー.

questions.question: 大学の奨学金(しょうがくきん)に ＿応募＿ した。
questions.explanation:
応募 is read おうぼ and means "to apply (for a scholarship, contest, etc.)".
応募 (おうぼ) is an on-yomi compound: 応 (オウ, respond/apply) + 募 (ボ, recruit/solicit). Together the word means "to respond to a recruitment" — to apply or enter (a contest, scholarship, job offer, etc.). The sentence 「大学の奨学金に応募した」 means "I applied for the university scholarship." The reading おうぼ uses the on-yomi of both: オウ + ボ. The confusion zone is おうぼ vs おうも vs おうぼう — distractors replace ボ with モ (a wrong on-yomi) or add an extra long vowel (おうぼう). 募 (ボ) appears in: 公募 (こうぼ, public recruitment), 募集 (ぼしゅう, recruitment drive), 募る (つのる, to solicit/grow stronger).
✗ おうも misreads 募 as モ instead of ボ. 募 reads ボ, not モ. The voiced b-sound (ボ) is essential — mo is a completely different syllable.
✗ おうぼう adds a long vowel to 募, making it ボウ. The on-yomi of 募 is a short ボ (one mora), not the long ボウ (two morae). おうぼう is not a reading of 応募.
✗ おうもう combines both errors — the wrong vowel モ and the extra length ウ. Neither the Mo reading nor the extended vowel are correct for 募.
例: コンテストに応募 (おうぼ) したら、二次審査 (にじしんさ) に進 (すす) めた。 — After applying to the contest, I was able to advance to the second round.

opts: ✔ おうぼ – 応募, ứng tuyển, nộp đơn xin (ỨNG MỘ)
おうも – không có từ này
おうぼう – 横暴 'ngang ngược', không phải chữ này
おうもう – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tôi đã nộp đơn xin học bổng của trường đại học.
ex.note: ỨNG MỘ. 募 đọc ぼ, âm ngắn, không có trường âm; 募集 (ぼしゅう) cùng chữ.

questions.question: 試験の成績(せいせき)が ＿発表＿ された。
questions.explanation:
発表 is read はっぴょう because 発 undergoes a sokuon contraction to はっ and 表 takes the on-yomi ひょう, voiced to ぴょう after the small っ.
発表 (はっぴょう) means "announcement" or "presentation." The reading requires understanding two phonological rules at once. First, 発 (はつ/ほつ) has an on-yomi はつ, but when it precedes a syllable beginning with ひ/は, the つ contracts into a sokuon っ: はつ + ひょう → はっひょう → はっぴょう. Second, after the glottal stop っ, the following consonant voices: ひょう becomes ぴょう. So the full chain is: は + っ + ぴょう = はっぴょう. This sokuon voicing pattern also appears in other words like 発表 (はっぴょう), 発見 (はっけん, discovery), and 発音 (はつおん, pronunciation — here no contraction because 音 begins with お). The character 表 (ひょう/おもて) means "to show" or "surface/table." It appears in 時刻表 (じこくひょう, timetable) and 代表 (だいひょう, representative). The sentence says: "The exam results 成績 (せいせき) were announced 発表 (はっぴょう)." 発表する is the standard verb for announcing or presenting information formally.
✗ はっひょう keeps the initial ひ unvoiced after the sokuon っ. In Japanese phonology, a voiceless consonant following っ typically voices to its pair: ひ → ぴ, は → ぱ, etc. はっひょう is phonologically non-standard and does not reflect the actual pronunciation.
✗ はっひょ drops the long vowel う from ひょう. The on-yomi of 表 is ひょう (a two-mora syllable ひょ + う). Shortening it to はっひょ removes the final mora and produces a non-existent reading.
✗ はっぴょ applies the correct voicing (ひ → ぴ) but drops the trailing long vowel う from ぴょう. The full on-yomi is ぴょう (three morae: ぴ + ょ + う), not the two-mora ぴょ.
例: 来週、プロジェクトの結果 (けっか) を発表 (はっぴょう) する予定 (よてい) です。 — We plan to announce the project results next week.

opts: はっひょう – không có từ này
✔ はっぴょう – 発表, công bố, phát biểu (PHÁT BIỂU)
はっひょ – không có từ này
はっぴょ – thiếu trường âm, sai
ex.trans: Kết quả kỳ thi đã được công bố.
ex.note: PHÁT BIỂU. 発 + 表 → はつ biến thành はっ, ひょう hóa thành ぴょう sau っ (như 出発 しゅっぱつ).

questions.question: 1 今年の夏は、 ＿過去＿ 十年間で一番の暑さだったそうだ。
questions.explanation:
過去 is read かこ because 過 takes on-yomi か and 去 takes on-yomi こ, forming the short compound meaning "the past."
過去 (かこ) means "the past" — time that has already elapsed. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 過 (か) = to pass, and 去 (こ) = to go away/leave. Together they describe time that has passed and gone. The sentence says: "This summer, the heat is apparently the worst in the past ten years." 過去十年間で一番の暑さ = "the hottest in the past ten years." This uses 過去 (かこ) in the common expression 過去○年間 (かこ○ねんかん, over the past ○ years). This is a second question testing the same reading かこ — see also entry hash 6b7589ae01efd5f7, which used a different sentence context (remembering things from the past). The core reading remains かこ: both morae are short, with no long vowels. The reading trap of adding long vowels (かきょ, かこう, かきょう) is the same. Here, the sentence context (hottest in ten years) reinforces the temporal past-reference use of 過去.
✗ かきょ uses the alternative on-yomi きょ for 去. In 過去, 去 reads こ (short), not きょ (used in 去年 きょねん, last year). The reading split of 去 is こ (in 過去) vs きょ (in 去年).
✗ かこう adds a long vowel to 去, producing こう instead of こ. 去 reads the single mora こ in 過去 — no long vowel is added.
✗ かきょう combines both the きょ reading of 去 and an added long vowel う. Both changes are wrong: 去 reads こ in 過去, and there is no long vowel.
例: 過去 (かこ) の失敗 (しっぱい) を教訓 (きょうくん) にして、今後 (こんご) に活 (い) かしたい。 — I want to learn from past failures and use them going forward.

opts: かきょ – không có từ này
かこう – 加工 'gia công', không phải chữ này
✔ かこ – 過去, quá khứ (QUÁ KHỨ)
かきょう – không có từ này
ex.trans: Nghe nói mùa hè năm nay nóng nhất trong mười năm qua.
ex.note: QUÁ KHỨ. 去 đọc こ (như 去年 きょねん), không có trường âm; đừng nhầm với 加工 かこう.

questions.question: 2 あと５分で東京駅に ＿到着＿ します
questions.explanation:
到着 is read とうちゃく — 到 reads とう and 着 reads ちゃく, meaning "arrival".
到着 (とうちゃく) = arrival. 「あと5分 (ふん) で東京駅 (とうきょうえき) に到着 (とうちゃく) します」 — "We will arrive at Tokyo Station in 5 minutes." 到 reads unvoiced とう (not voiced どう).
✗ とうつく: correct とう for 到 but kun-yomi つく for 着. In 到着, 着 takes on-yomi ちゃく.
✗ どうつく: voices 到 to どう (wrong) and uses kun-yomi つく for 着 (wrong).
✗ どうちゃく: correct ちゃく for 着 but voices 到 to どう (wrong).
例: 飛行機 (ひこうき) は30分 (さんじゅっぷん) 遅 (おく) れて到着 (とうちゃく) した。 — The airplane arrived 30 minutes late.

opts: とうつく – lẫn âm kun つく của 着, sai
✔ とうちゃく – 到着, đến nơi (ĐÁO TRƯỚC)
どうつく – không có từ này
どうちゃく – không có từ này
ex.trans: Còn 5 phút nữa là đến ga Tokyo.
ex.note: ĐÁO TRƯỚC. 到 đọc とう (âm trong, không đục), 着 trong từ ghép đọc ちゃく.

questions.question: 3 公園の木の枝を ＿折って＿ はいけません。
questions.explanation:
折って is read おって, meaning "break off / snap" — breaking branches in a park is prohibited.
折る (おる) means "to break off," "to snap," or "to fold." Its te-form 折って (おって) is used in compound instructions or descriptions. The sentence says: "You must not break 折って (おって) the branches of park trees." 公園の木の枝を折ってはいけません = "Do not snap branches off park trees" is a public rules sign. The kanji 折 uses the kun-yomi お in the transitive verb form: 折る (おる, you snap something). The intransitive counterpart is 折れる (おれる, it snaps by itself). Its on-yomi せつ appears in 骨折 (こっせつ, bone fracture) and 折衷 (せっちゅう, compromise). The four distractors — うって (売る, to sell/hit), おって (correct), わって (割る, to break/split), and きって (切る, to cut) — all describe destructive or ending actions on objects. The crucial distinction: 折る (fold/snap at a joint), 割る (crack/split into pieces), and 切る (cut with a blade). Tree branches are snapped (折る), not cut (切る) or split (割る).
✗ うって is the te-form of either 売る (うる, to sell) or 打つ (うつ, to hit/strike). Selling or hitting tree branches are different actions. 折 does not read うって.
✗ わって is the te-form of 割る (わる), meaning "to split" or "to crack." Breaking a branch means snapping it (折る), not splitting it into pieces (割る). 折 does not read わって.
✗ きって is the te-form of 切る (きる), meaning "to cut." Cutting uses a sharp instrument; snapping a branch uses force at a joint. These are different actions. 折 does not read きって.
例: 祖母 (そぼ) が庭 (にわ) の花 (はな) を折 (お) って花瓶 (かびん) に飾 (かざ) ってくれた。 — My grandmother snapped off some flowers from the garden and arranged them in a vase.

opts: うって – 売って/打って 'bán/đánh', không phải chữ này
✔ おって – 折って, bẻ, gấp (CHIẾT)
わって – 割って 'làm vỡ, chia', không phải chữ này
きって – 切って 'cắt', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Không được bẻ cành cây trong công viên.
ex.note: CHIẾT. 折る (おる) = bẻ gãy, gấp; 折れる = bị gãy. Phân biệt với 割る (vỡ) và 切る (cắt).

questions.question: 4 インターネットで最新の ＿情報＿ をチェックした。
questions.explanation:
情報 is read じょうほう — 情 reads じょう and 報 reads ほう, meaning "information".
情報 (じょうほう) = information/data. 情 (じょう) = feelings/circumstances, 報 (ほう) = to report. 「インターネットで最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) をチェックした」 — "I checked the latest information on the internet."
✗ じゅうほう: じゅう for 情 is wrong. 情 reads じょう. じゅう belongs to 十 (ten) or 重 (heavy).
✗ じょうほ: shortens ほう to ほ. 報 reads ほう (long vowel), not ほ.
✗ じゅうほ: wrong じゅう for 情 and wrong ほ for 報.
例: 最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) はウェブサイトで確認 (かくにん) できます。 — You can check the latest information on the website.

opts: じゅうほう – không có từ này
じょうほ – thiếu trường âm, sai
✔ じょうほう – 情報, thông tin (TÌNH BÁO)
じゅうほ – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tôi đã kiểm tra thông tin mới nhất trên internet.
ex.note: TÌNH BÁO. Cả hai âm đều dài: じょう・ほう. 情 còn gặp trong 感情 (かんじょう), 事情 (じじょう).

questions.question: 5 最近、野菜の ＿値段＿ が高くなっています。
questions.explanation:
値段 is read ねだん and means "price".
値段 (ねだん) means "price" or "cost". The compound uses a mix of readings: 値 (ね, value/price — kun-yomi) + 段 (だん, step/grade — here the on-yomi DAN softens to だん). The sentence 「最近、野菜の値段が高くなっています」 means "The prices of vegetables have been rising recently." The reading challenge is ね for 値 — the on-yomi of 値 is チ (e.g., 価値 かち, value/worth), but in 値段 the kun-yomi ね is used. The voiced だん for 段 (normally タン in formal compounds like 段階 だんかい) here uses a lighter, kun-like reading common in everyday compounds. Distractors かかく (価格, formal price) and かがく (科学, science) share similar sounds but are different words.
✗ かかく (価格) means "price" in a more formal/economic register. 価格 uses entirely different kanji — 価 (カ, value) + 格 (カク, standard/grade). It is a real synonym of 値段 but is not a reading of 値段.
✗ かがく (科学) means "science" or (化学, chemistry). It is phonetically close to かかく but refers to a completely different domain — not price at all.
✗ ねたん is a near-miss that misreads 段 as タン instead of the correct voiced だん. In 値段, 段 takes the voiced reading だん, not the unvoiced タン.
例: 旬 (しゅん) の時期 (じき) は野菜 (やさい) の値段 (ねだん) が下 (さ) がるので、たくさん買 (か) っておく。 — When vegetables are in season, their prices drop, so I buy a lot.

opts: かかく – 価格 'giá cả', không phải chữ này
かがく – 科学/化学 'khoa học/hóa học', không phải chữ này
ねたん – thiếu âm đục, sai
✔ ねだん – 値段, giá tiền (TRỊ ĐOẠN)
ex.trans: Dạo này giá rau đang đắt lên.
ex.note: TRỊ ĐOẠN. 値 (ね) = giá trị, 段 (だん) đọc đục. 値段が高い/安い. Đồng nghĩa với 価格 (trang trọng hơn).

questions.question: 6 彼はあの国の文化に ＿深い＿ 関心を持っている。
questions.explanation:
深い is read ふかい and means "deep" — describing a deep interest in that country's culture.
深 (ふか) い is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "deep". The sentence 「彼はあの国の文化に深い関心を持っている」 means "He has a deep interest in that country's culture." In Japanese, 深い (ふかい) extends beyond physical depth — it also describes intensity of feeling, interest, or understanding, much like English "deep". The kun-yomi ふか is the only reading used when 深 appears alone as an adjective. The on-yomi シン appears in compounds: 深夜 (しんや, late night), 深刻 (しんこく, serious/grave), 深海 (しんかい, deep sea). The 氵 (water) radical visually signals something related to depth.
✗ つよい is the reading of 強い, meaning "strong". A strong interest and a deep interest are related but 強 and 深 are different kanji; 深 does not read つよ.
✗ ひろい is the reading of 広い, meaning "wide / broad". A broad interest and a deep interest overlap in meaning, but 広 (ひろい, wide) and 深 (ふかい, deep) are distinct adjectives with different kanji.
✗ おもい is the reading of 重い, meaning "heavy" or "serious". While 重い can sometimes describe a serious matter, it does not pair with 関心 (かんしん, interest) in this way; 深い is the standard collocate for 関心.
例: この問題 (もんだい) については、深 (ふか) く考 (かんが) える必要 (ひつよう) がある。 — We need to think deeply about this issue.

opts: ✔ ふかい – 深い, sâu, sâu sắc (THÂM)
つよい – 強い 'mạnh', không phải chữ này
ひろい – 広い 'rộng', không phải chữ này
おもい – 重い 'nặng', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Anh ấy có mối quan tâm sâu sắc đến văn hóa của nước đó.
ex.note: THÂM. 深い = sâu (nước, ý nghĩa): 深い関心, 深い海. Trái nghĩa 浅い (あさい).

questions.question: 7 昨日、友達に本を ＿返しました＿ 。
questions.explanation:
返しました is read かえしました and means "returned" — the speaker returned a book to a friend.
返す (かえす) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to return (something) to its owner". The polite past form 返しました (かえしました) expresses the completed act of giving something back. The sentence 「昨日、友達に本を返しました」 means "Yesterday, I returned a book to my friend." The kanji 返 contains the 辶 (movement) radical and the component 反 (reverse/against), visually suggesting movement back to the origin. Its on-yomi ヘン appears in: 返答 (へんとう, reply), 返金 (へんきん, refund), 返済 (へんさい, repayment). The verb 返す is transitive — the speaker returns something — as opposed to 帰る (かえる, to go back), which is intransitive.
✗ かしました is the polite past form of 貸す (かす), meaning "to lend". Lending a book and returning a book are opposite actions — lending is giving someone else temporary use; returning is giving it back.
✗ もどしました is the polite past form of 戻す (もどす), meaning "to put back / to restore". While 戻す and 返す both relate to putting things back, 返す specifically means returning something to its owner, while 戻す means restoring to a previous state or location.
✗ わたしました is the polite past form of 渡す (わたす), meaning "to hand over / to pass". Handing something over and returning it to an owner are different — 渡す is a general transfer while 返す specifically completes a loan.
例: 借 (か) りた傘 (かさ) を返 (かえ) さないままにしていて、相手 (あいて) に申 (もう) し訳 (わけ) なかった。 — I felt bad for not returning the umbrella I had borrowed.

opts: かしました – 貸しました 'cho mượn', không phải chữ này
✔ かえしました – 返しました, trả lại (PHẢN)
もどしました – 戻しました 'để lại chỗ cũ', không phải chữ này
わたしました – 渡しました 'đưa', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Hôm qua tôi đã trả sách cho bạn.
ex.note: PHẢN. 返す (かえす) = trả lại; 帰る (かえる) = về nhà, 変える = thay đổi. Cùng âm かえ, khác chữ.

questions.question: 8 月の ＿表面＿ はでこぼこしている。
questions.explanation:
表面 is read ひょうめん — 表 reads ひょう and 面 reads めん, meaning "surface".
表面 (ひょうめん) = surface — the outer face or exterior of something. 表 (ひょう) = outer surface/to show, 面 (めん) = face/surface. The sentence says 「月 (つき) の表面 (ひょうめん) はでこぼこしている」 — "The surface of the moon is bumpy." Both kanji have long vowels in their on-yomi: 表 is ひょう (three morae) and 面 is めん (two morae). The trap is shortening either to しょ or ひょ.
✗ しょめん: wrong しょ for 表. 表 reads ひょう, not しょ. しょ could fit kanji like 書 (しょ, writing) or 所 (しょ, place).
✗ ひょめん: shortens 表 to ひょ, dropping the final う. 表 reads ひょう (three morae, long vowel), not ひょ alone.
✗ しょうめん: wrong しょう for 表, though this reading looks like 正面 (しょうめん, front face) — a real word but not what is written here. 表 reads ひょう, not しょう.
例: この金属 (きんぞく) は表面 (ひょうめん) がなめらかで美 (うつく) しい。 — This metal has a smooth and beautiful surface.

opts: しょめん – 書面 'văn bản', không phải chữ này
ひょめん – thiếu trường âm, sai
しょうめん – 正面 'mặt trước', không phải chữ này
✔ ひょうめん – 表面, bề mặt (BIỂU DIỆN)
ex.trans: Bề mặt của mặt trăng gồ ghề.
ex.note: BIỂU DIỆN. 表 đọc ひょう có trường âm (発表 はっぴょう); 面 đọc めん. Trái nghĩa 裏面 (りめん).

questions.question: １ スポーツで ＿汗＿ をかいたので、シャワーをあびた。
questions.explanation:
汗 is read あせ and means "sweat" — worked up a sweat playing sports, then took a shower.
汗 (あせ) means "sweat" or "perspiration". The sentence 「スポーツで汗をかいたので、シャワーをあびた」 means "Because I sweated doing sports, I took a shower." 汗をかく (あせをかく) is the set phrase meaning "to sweat", where かく means "to produce/exude". The kanji 汗 contains the 氵 (water) radical, consistent with its meaning of a liquid produced by the body. The on-yomi カン appears in compounds like 発汗 (はっかん, perspiration/sweating). When 汗 stands alone as a noun, it always reads あせ. The four options test whether learners distinguish body fluids and substances: sweat (あせ), garbage (ごみ), dirt (よごれ), tears (なみだ).
✗ ごみ means "garbage" or "trash" — a non-liquid substance. Garbage and sweat are entirely different things. ごみ is typically written in hiragana or with the kanji 塵 or 芥, not 汗.
✗ よごれ means "dirt" or "a stain" — what is left on something after it gets soiled. Dirt and sweat are related (sweating can cause dirt) but are distinct; 汗 does not read よごれ.
✗ なみだ is the reading of 涙 (tears). Tears and sweat are both bodily liquids from the 氵 radical family, but they come from different body parts and different stimuli. 汗 does not read なみだ.
例: 夏 (なつ) に走 (はし) ると大 (おお) 量 (りょう) の汗 (あせ) をかくので、水分 (すいぶん) を十分 (じゅうぶん) に補給 (ほきゅう) する必要 (ひつよう) がある。 — Running in summer makes you sweat a lot, so you need to stay well hydrated.

opts: ✔ あせ – 汗, mồ hôi (HÃN)
ごみ – rác, không phải chữ này
よごれ – 汚れ 'vết bẩn', không phải chữ này
なみだ – 涙 'nước mắt', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Chơi thể thao đổ mồ hôi nên tôi đã đi tắm.
ex.note: HÃN. 汗 (あせ) = 氵 + 干; 汗をかく = đổ mồ hôi (dùng かく, không dùng 出る). (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ２ このお知らせをみんなに ＿配って＿ ください。
questions.explanation:
配って is read くばって, meaning "distribute / hand out" — the instruction is to distribute a notice to everyone.
配る (くばる) means "to distribute," "to hand out," or "to deliver" — giving something to multiple people one by one. Its te-form 配って (くばって) appears in instructions. The sentence says: "Please distribute 配って (くばって) this notice お知らせ to everyone." みんなに配る = "to hand out to everyone" is a typical classroom or meeting instruction. The kanji 配 uses the kun-yomi くば in verb form. Its on-yomi はい appears in compounds like 配達 (はいたつ, delivery), 配布 (はいふ, distribution/circulation), and 心配 (しんぱい, worry/concern). Note 心配 (しんぱい, worry) — 配 in this compound means distributing one's heart/mind (a figurative use). The distractors — だまって (keeping silent), もらって (receiving), and はらって (paying) — are all te-form verbs that could naturally appear in social or transactional contexts, but none means distributing.
✗ だまって is the te-form of 黙る (だまる), meaning "to keep silent" or "to be quiet." Distributing a notice requires action; keeping silent is the opposite of actively handing things out. 配 does not read だまって.
✗ もらって is the te-form of もらう, meaning "to receive" (as a favor from someone). Receiving is the opposite direction from distributing. 配 does not read もらって.
✗ はらって is the te-form of 払う (はらう), meaning "to pay." Paying for something and distributing something are different transactions. 配 does not read はらって.
例: 会議 (かいぎ) の前 (まえ) に資料 (しりょう) を参加者 (さんかしゃ) に配 (くば) っておいた。 — Before the meeting, I distributed the materials to the participants.

opts: だまって – 黙って 'im lặng', không phải chữ này
もらって – 'nhận', không phải chữ này
はらって – 払って 'trả tiền', không phải chữ này
✔ くばって – 配って, phát, phân phát (PHỐI)
ex.trans: Hãy phát thông báo này cho mọi người.
ex.note: PHỐI. 配る (くばる) = phát cho từng người; 配達 (はいたつ) giao hàng, 心配 (しんぱい). (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ３ 新しい道路がもうすぐ ＿完成＿ するそうだ。
questions.explanation:
完成 is read かんせい and means "completion" — a new road will be finished soon.
完成 (かんせい) is an on-yomi compound: 完 (カン, complete/whole) + 成 (セイ, accomplish/become). Together the word means "full accomplishment" — reaching a completed state. The sentence 「新しい道路がもうすぐ完成するそうだ」 means "I heard that the new road will be completed soon." The reading challenge is distinguishing かんせい (完成, completion) from other similarly-sounding compounds: けんせつ (建設, construction), かんぜん (完全, perfect), けんちく (建築, architecture). All four relate to buildings and construction, making them contextually plausible but semantically distinct. 完 appears in: 完了 (かんりょう, completion/finishing), 完全 (かんぜん, perfection).
✗ けんせつ (建設) means "construction" — the process of building. 建 (ケン, build) + 設 (セツ, establish). A road under construction would use 建設中, while 完成 describes the finished result.
✗ かんぜん (完全) means "perfect" or "complete (without flaws)". 完 (カン) + 全 (ゼン, all/complete). 完全 describes a state of perfection; 完成 describes the act of finishing/completing a project.
✗ けんちく (建築) means "architecture" or "the act of constructing a building". 建 (ケン) + 築 (チク, build/construct). Architecture and completion are related but different stages — 建築 is the activity, 完成 is the outcome.
例: 3年 (さんねん) かけて書 (か) いた小説 (しょうせつ) がついに完成 (かんせい) した。 — The novel I spent three years writing was finally completed.

opts: ✔ かんせい – 完成, hoàn thành (HOÀN THÀNH)
けんせつ – 建設 'xây dựng', không phải chữ này
かんぜん – 完全 'hoàn toàn', không phải chữ này
けんちく – 建築 'kiến trúc', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Nghe nói con đường mới sắp hoàn thành.
ex.note: HOÀN THÀNH. 完 (かん) = xong, 成 (せい) = thành. Phân biệt 完成 (hoàn thành) và 完全 (hoàn toàn). (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ４ ここから ＿島＿ がたくさん見えますよ。
questions.explanation:
島 is read しま, meaning "island" — from here, many islands are visible.
島 (しま) means "island" — a landmass surrounded by water. The sentence says: "From here, you can see many islands 島 (しま)!" ここから島がたくさん見える is a natural sight-seeing expression, especially in Japan with its many island chains. The kanji 島 uses the kun-yomi しま when standing alone as a noun. Its on-yomi とう appears in compounds like 半島 (はんとう, peninsula), 島国 (しまぐに, island nation), and 列島 (れっとう, archipelago). Japan itself is often called 島国 (しまぐに) because it is an island nation. The four distractors — ほし (star), とり (bird), しま (correct), and うま (horse) — are four common noun readings that share no visual connection to the kanji 島. This tests direct kanji-reading recognition, as the distractors describe entirely different things (celestial body, animal, island, animal).
✗ ほし is the reading of 星 (ほし), meaning "star." Stars and islands are both scattered across vast spaces (sky/sea), but 島 does not read ほし. The kanji 星 and 島 look completely different.
✗ とり is the reading of 鳥 (とり), meaning "bird." The kanji 島 does contain a bird-like component (鳥 is embedded visually), but 島 itself reads しま (island), not とり (bird). The radical origin does not change the reading.
✗ うま is the reading of 馬 (うま), meaning "horse." Horse and island have nothing in common. 島 does not read うま.
例: この地域 (ちいき) には大 (おお) きな島 (しま) が一つと、小 (ちい) さな島 (しま) がいくつかある。 — This area has one large island and several smaller islands.

opts: ほし – 星 'ngôi sao', không phải chữ này
とり – 鳥 'chim', không phải chữ này
✔ しま – 島, đảo (ĐẢO)
うま – 馬 'ngựa', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Từ đây nhìn thấy nhiều hòn đảo lắm đấy.
ex.note: ĐẢO. 島 (しま) có 鳥 bớt nét ở trên, nên option 鳥 (とり) là bẫy. Âm on: とう (半島). (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ５ 田中さんはちょっと ＿困って＿ いるみたいです。
questions.explanation:
困って is read こまって and means "in trouble / struggling" — Tanaka seems to be having difficulty.
困る (こまる) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to be in trouble", "to be troubled", or "to struggle with something". The te-form 困って (こまって) connects with いる to express the ongoing state: 「田中さんはちょっと困っているみたいです」 — "It seems Tanaka is having a bit of trouble." The kanji 困 contains the 囗 (enclosure) radical around the 木 (tree) component — visually, a tree stuck inside a box, unable to grow. This is a perfect visual mnemonic for being stuck or in a difficult situation. The on-yomi コン appears in: 困難 (こんなん, difficulty/hardship), 困惑 (こんわく, confusion/perplexity).
✗ まよって is the te-form of 迷う (まよう), meaning "to get lost / to be indecisive". Being uncertain what to do and being in trouble are related feelings, but 困 does not read まよ.
✗ おこって is the te-form of 怒る (おこる), meaning "to get angry". Being angry and being troubled are different emotional states; 困 does not read おこ.
✗ うたがって is the te-form of 疑う (うたがう), meaning "to doubt / to suspect". Suspecting someone and being in trouble are different; 困 does not read うたが.
例: 道 (みち) に迷 (まよ) って困 (こま) っていたら、親切 (しんせつ) な人 (ひと) が案内 (あんない) してくれた。 — When I was lost and in trouble, a kind person showed me the way.

opts: まよって – 迷って 'lạc, phân vân', không phải chữ này
✔ こまって – 困って, gặp rắc rối, khó xử (KHỐN)
おこって – 怒って 'giận', không phải chữ này
うたがって – 疑って 'nghi ngờ', không phải chữ này
ex.trans: Anh Tanaka có vẻ đang hơi gặp rắc rối.
ex.note: KHỐN. 困る (こまる) = gặp khó, khó xử; 困難 (こんなん). Nhớ hình 木 bị nhốt trong 囗. (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ６ ＿平日＿ は午後8 時まで開いています。
questions.explanation:
平日 is read へいじつ and means "a weekday" (as opposed to a weekend or holiday).
平日 (へいじつ) is an on-yomi compound: 平 (ヘイ, ordinary/level) + 日 (ジツ, day). Together the word means "an ordinary day" — i.e., Monday through Friday, as opposed to 休日 (きゅうじつ, day off) or 休みの日. The sentence 「平日は午後8時まで開いています」 means "On weekdays, (we) are open until 8 p.m." The phonological trap is the same as in 休日 — 日 reads ジツ (not にち) when it is the second element in certain time compounds. The distractor へいにち would be a mistake of reading 日 as にち in this compound context. The first kanji 平 reads ヘイ here, not ほん (which belongs to 本).
✗ ほんにち (本日) — wait, this option is ほんにち, which would come from 本日 (ほんじつ, today — formal). But here the first kanji is 平 (ヘイ, ordinary), not 本 (ほん/ホン). So ほんにち misidentifies both the first kanji reading and the second kanji reading.
✗ へいにち misreads 日 as にち. In the compound 平日, 日 uses the on-yomi ジツ, not にち. へいにち is not a standard reading of this compound.
✗ ほんじつ (本日) is a real word meaning "today" (formal), but it is a different word. Its first kanji is 本 (ほん, this/book), not 平 (へい, ordinary). The compound in the question is 平日, not 本日.
例: この図書館 (としょかん) は平日 (へいじつ) のみ開 (あ) いていて、土日 (どにち) は休 (やす) みです。 — This library is open only on weekdays and is closed on Saturdays and Sundays.

opts: ほんにち – không có từ này
へいにち – không có từ này
ほんじつ – 本日 'hôm nay', không phải chữ này
✔ へいじつ – 平日, ngày thường (BÌNH NHẬT)
ex.trans: Ngày thường mở cửa đến 8 giờ tối.
ex.note: BÌNH NHẬT. 平 đọc へい (平和 へいわ), 日 đọc じつ ở đây. 平日 ↔ 週末/休日. (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng thực ra là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ７ わたしは3年前に大学を ＿卒業＿ しました。
questions.explanation:
卒業 is read そつぎょう because 卒 takes on-yomi そつ and 業 takes on-yomi ぎょう, forming the standard word for "graduation."
卒業 (そつぎょう) means "graduation" — completing a course of study at a school. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 卒 (そつ) = to finish/graduate, and 業 (ぎょう) = undertaking/work/studies. Together 卒業 describes completing (卒) one's educational undertaking (業). The sentence says: "I graduated 卒業 (そつぎょう) from university three years ago." 大学を卒業する = "to graduate from university" is the standard phrase. The reading challenge: 卒 must be そつ (unvoiced, two morae), not the voiced さつ or the short forms そつぎょ. 業 must be ぎょう (voiced, long vowel), not the unvoiced きょう or the shortened ぎょ. The four options systematically cover: そつぎょう (correct), さつぎょう (voiced beginning), そつぎょ (missing long vowel), and さつぎょ (both wrong). 卒 also appears in 卒業式 (そつぎょうしき, graduation ceremony) and 卒業生 (そつぎょうせい, graduate). 業 also appears in 授業 (じゅぎょう, class), 就業 (しゅうぎょう, employment), and 残業 (ざんぎょう, overtime).
✗ さつぎょう voices 卒 to さつ. 卒 reads そつ (unvoiced), not さつ (voiced). さつ is the reading of 殺 (kill) or 冊 (volume) — not 卒.
✗ さつぎょ voices 卒 and drops the long vowel from 業. Both changes are wrong: 卒 = そつ (unvoiced), 業 = ぎょう (long vowel). さつぎょ is a double error.
✗ そつぎょ reads 卒 correctly as そつ but drops the trailing long vowel from 業. 業 reads ぎょう (three morae: ぎ + ょ + う), not the shorter ぎょ (two morae). The long vowel is essential.
例: 彼 (かれ) は今年 (ことし) 大学院 (だいがくいん) を卒業 (そつぎょう) して、外資系企業 (がいしけいきぎょう) に就職 (しゅうしょく) した。 — He graduated from graduate school this year and got a job at a foreign-affiliated company.

opts: さつぎょう – không có từ này
✔ そつぎょう – 卒業, tốt nghiệp (TỐT NGHIỆP)
さつぎょ – không có từ này
そつぎょ – thiếu trường âm, sai
ex.trans: Tôi tốt nghiệp đại học 3 năm trước.
ex.note: TỐT NGHIỆP. 卒 đọc そつ (không phải さつ); 業 đọc ぎょう có trường âm. 卒業式 lễ tốt nghiệp. (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: ８ びんのふたは ＿固く＿ しめておいてください。
questions.explanation:
固く is read かたく because 固 takes the kun-yomi かた, meaning "firmly / tightly," which matches tightening a bottle lid.
固い (かたい) is an i-adjective meaning "hard, firm, or tight." Its adverbial form 固く (かたく) means "firmly" or "tightly." The kanji 固 carries the idea of something set, hardened, or not easily moved. The sentence says: "Please close the bottle lid firmly." 固く (かたく) fits perfectly here because it describes the manner of tightening — not lightly, not loosely, but with a firm grip. The kun-yomi かた is the reading used when 固 stands alone as a verb or adjective stem: 固い (かたい, hard/firm), 固める (かためる, to harden/solidify). The on-yomi こ appears in compounds like 固定 (こてい, fixation) and 固体 (こたい, solid substance). In adjective-adverb use like this sentence, kun-yomi かた is always correct. The adverbial suffix く attached to かたい produces かたく, changing the i-adjective to an adverb modifying the verb しめる (to close/tighten).
✗ かるく is the adverbial form of 軽い (かるい), meaning "lightly." Closing a lid lightly would be the opposite of what the sentence instructs.
✗ ゆるく is the adverbial form of 緩い (ゆるい), meaning "loosely." A loosely closed lid defeats the purpose of the instruction — contents could spill or air could get in.
✗ きつく is the adverbial form of きつい, meaning "tight" or "strict." While close in nuance to かたく, the underlined kanji is 固く, not きつく. きつい is typically written in kana and does not use the kanji 固. The question tests the reading of 固, not a vocabulary substitution.
例: この機械 (きかい) のネジは固 (かた) く締 (し) めてある。 — The screw on this machine is fastened firmly.

opts: かるく – 軽く 'nhẹ', không phải chữ này
ゆるく – 緩く 'lỏng', trái nghĩa, không phải chữ này
きつく – 'chặt', không viết bằng chữ này
✔ かたく – 固く, chặt, cứng (CỐ)
ex.trans: Hãy đóng chặt nắp chai.
ex.note: CỐ. 固い (かたい) = cứng, chặt; 硬い (bộ đá) và 堅い cũng đọc かたい. ふたを固く閉める = đóng nắp chặt. (?) Đề gắn nhãn orthography nhưng là câu hỏi cách đọc.

questions.question: 今月は ＿休日が＿ 多かった。
questions.explanation:
休日 is read きゅうじつ (here きゅうじっ) and means "holiday / day off".
休日 (きゅうじつ) is an on-yomi compound: 休 (キュウ, rest) + 日 (ジツ, day). Together they mean "a rest day" or "a day off". The sentence says 「今月は休日が多かった」 — "This month had many holidays." Both kanji use their on-yomi: キュウ + ジツ. Note that before a voiced syllable, the ジツ can be heard as じっ depending on pitch pattern, which is reflected in the correct answer. The on-yomi ジツ for 日 appears when 日 is the second element in a time-related compound, as seen also in 本日 (ほんじつ, today, formal) and 祝日 (しゅくじつ, public holiday). This vowel alternation — にち vs ジツ — is a key N3 reading challenge.
✗ しゅくじつ (祝日, national holiday) is a real word but uses a different kanji — 祝 (しゅく, celebrate) instead of 休 (きゅう, rest). 休日 and 祝日 are related but not the same: 休日 is any day off, while 祝日 is specifically a public holiday.
✗ きゅうにち does not exist as a standard compound. The second kanji 日 in time compounds reads ジツ (not にち) when it follows キュウ in this pairing. にち appears in words like 毎日 (まいにち) where the pattern is different.
✗ しゅくにち is not a standard word either. It mismatches 祝 with a wrong reading of 日 (にち instead of じつ). This option tries to combine two wrong readings at once.
例: 今週 (こんしゅう) は休日 (きゅうじつ) が二日 (ふつか) あるので、旅行 (りょこう) の計画 (けいかく) を立 (た) てた。 — This week has two days off, so I made plans for a trip.

opts: しゅくじった – không có từ này
✔ きゅうじつ – 休日, ngày nghỉ (HƯU NHẬT)
きゅうにち – không có từ này
しゅくにち – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tháng này có nhiều ngày nghỉ.
ex.note: HƯU NHẬT. 休 đọc きゅう (休憩, 休暇); 日 đọc じつ (平日, 祝日 しゅくじつ). Option 2 trong đề bị cắt, đúng là きゅうじつ.

questions.question: 山口(やまぐち)さんに束京(とうきょう)を ＿あんない＿ してもらった。
questions.explanation:
あんない is written 案内 — the kanji 案 (plan/proposal) plus 内 (inside/guide).
案内 (あんない) means "to guide" or "to show around". The kanji 案 (アン) carries the idea of a plan or a proposal; 内 (ナイ) means "inside" or "within". Together they form a word for showing someone the way through an unfamiliar space, literally "a guide from the inside". The sentence says Yamaguchi-san guided the speaker around Tokyo (東京, とうきょう). The verb form is 案内する (あんないする), so あんないしてもらった means "had (someone) guide me around". Among the four options, only 案内 uses the correct kanji for both sounds: ア for 案 and ナイ for 内. The other three options mix in wrong characters.
✗ 安内 uses 安 (アン, peaceful/cheap) instead of 案 (アン, plan/guide). The sound is the same — アン — but 安 never carries the meaning of guiding or showing around.
✗ 家内 reads かない, not あんない. 家内 (かない) is an old-fashioned word for "one's wife". The reading of 家 here is か, not あん.
✗ 室内 reads しつない, meaning "indoors" or "interior of a room". It is a real compound word, but its reading is completely different from あんない, and its meaning has nothing to do with guiding someone.
例: 受付 (うけつけ) の人 (ひと) が会議室 (かいぎしつ) まで案内 (あんない) してくれた。 — The receptionist guided us to the conference room.

opts: 安内 – không có từ này (安 AN)
家内 – かない 'vợ (của tôi)', đọc khác
室内 – しつない 'trong phòng', đọc khác
✔ 案内 – あんない, hướng dẫn, dẫn đi (ÁN NỘI)
ex.trans: Tôi được anh Yamaguchi dẫn đi tham quan Tokyo.
ex.note: 案 (ÁN) = 安 + 木, có cây ở dưới. 安 (AN) chỉ là 'yên ổn'. 案内する = hướng dẫn, chỉ đường.

questions.question: 9 東京は ＿げんざい＿ 午後３時です。
questions.explanation:
げんざい is written 現在 because 現 means "present/current" and 在 means "to exist/to be present," together meaning "right now / the present time."
現在 (げんざい) means "the present time" or "currently" — it is used to indicate the current moment or current state of affairs. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 現 (げん) = present/actual/to appear, and 在 (ざい) = to exist/to be located. Together they mean "existing in the present moment." The sentence says: "It is currently 現在 (げんざい) 3:00 PM in Tokyo." This is a typical announcement or news broadcast phrasing. The key distinctions are 現 (げん, present/actual) vs 視 (し, to look/observe) for the first kanji, and 在 (ざい, to exist) vs 存 (そん/ぞん, to exist/preserve) for the second. 現 appears in 現在 (げんざい), 現実 (げんじつ, reality), and 現代 (げんだい, modern times). 在 appears in 現在 (げんざい), 存在 (そんざい, existence), and 在宅 (ざいたく, being home). 視 appears in 視力 (しりょく, eyesight) and 視野 (しや, field of vision). 存 appears in 存在 (そんざい) and 生存 (せいぞん, survival).
✗ 視在 uses 視 (し, to look/observe) instead of 現 (げん, present/actual). 視 is used in sight-related words like 視力 (しりょく, eyesight). It does not mean "current" or "present time" and does not read げん.
✗ 現存 has the correct first kanji 現 (げん) but uses 存 (そん/ぞん) instead of 在 (ざい). 現存 (げんそん) is actually a real word meaning "still in existence" (as in a historical artifact that still exists today), but it means existential persistence, not "the current time/currently."
✗ 視存 combines 視 (look/observe) and 存 (exist/preserve) — both wrong kanji. 視存 is not a real word. Neither character matches the meaning or reading of 現在.
例: 現在 (げんざい) の状況 (じょうきょう) を報告 (ほうこく) します。 — I will report on the current situation.

opts: 視在 – không có từ này (視 THỊ = nhìn)
現存 – げんそん 'còn tồn tại', không hợp
✔ 現在 – げんざい, hiện tại, bây giờ (HIỆN TẠI)
視存 – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tokyo hiện tại là 3 giờ chiều.
ex.note: 現 (HIỆN) bộ 王 + 見; 視 (THỊ) bộ ネ + 見. 在 (TẠI) = ở, tồn tại; 存 (TỒN) là 'còn'.

questions.question: 10 こちらのサンプルは ＿ごじゆう＿ にお取りください。
questions.explanation:
ごじゆう is written ご自由 because 自 means "oneself/free" and 由 means "reason/basis," forming 自由 (freedom), with the honorific prefix ご.
自由 (じゆう) means "freedom" or "as you please." In the phrase ご自由にお取りください (ごじゆうにおとりください), it means "please take freely" or "help yourself." The word 自由 uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 自 (じ) = self, own, and 由 (ゆう) = reason, origin, or basis. Together they convey the idea of "acting on one's own accord" — freedom. The honorific prefix ご is added to make the phrase polite, as in ご自由に (ごじゆうに, please feel free to). The two kanji that learners must distinguish are 自 (self) vs 事 (matter/thing) for the first position, and 由 (reason/origin) vs 有 (to have/exist) for the second. 自有 and ご事由 are not standard compounds. 事由 (じゆう) is an actual legal/formal word meaning "reason" or "grounds," written with 事 (matter) + 由 (reason), but the underlined kana ごじゆう in the context of "take freely" calls for 自由 (freedom), not 事由 (formal reason).
✗ ご事有 uses 事 (matter/thing) for the first kanji and 有 (to have/exist) for the second. 事有 is not a real compound. 有 means "to have" or "existence" (有名 ゆうめい, famous) and does not combine with 事 to mean freedom.
✗ ご事由 uses 事 (matter/thing) instead of 自 (self). 事由 (じゆう) is a legal term meaning "grounds" or "reason," not "freedom." The context — helping yourself to samples — requires 自由 (freedom to act), not 事由 (formal reason).
✗ ご自有 uses 自 correctly for the first kanji but swaps 由 for 有 (to have/exist). 自有 is not a standard word. 由 (ゆう) means reason or origin and is the second kanji in 自由; replacing it with 有 breaks the compound.
例: このカフェでは、コーヒーのおかわりが自由 (じゆう) です。 — At this cafe, coffee refills are free (unlimited).

opts: ご事有 – không có từ này
ご事由 – じゆう 'lý do sự việc', đọc じゆう nhưng không hợp nghĩa
ご自有 – không có từ này
✔ ご自由 – ごじゆう, tự do, tùy ý (TỰ DO)
ex.trans: Xin quý khách cứ tự nhiên lấy hàng mẫu ở đây.
ex.note: 自 (TỰ) + 由 (DO). ご自由にお取りください là câu quen gặp ở cửa hàng. 由 bộ 田 thêm nét dọc thò lên.

questions.question: 11 大学では ＿ほうりつ＿ を勉強ました。
questions.explanation:
ほうりつ is written 法律 — 法 (law/method) + 律 (rule/regulation).
法律 (ほうりつ) means "law" in the legal sense — the body of rules governing society. Both kanji use on-yomi: 法 (ホウ, law/method) + 律 (リツ, rule/rhythm). Together they refer to enacted law (statutes). The sentence 「大学では法律を勉強しました」 means "I studied law at university." The trap is distinguishing 法 (ホウ) from 方 (ホウ), and 律 (リツ) from 立 (タツ). Both pairs share the same on-yomi (ホウ and リツ respectively), but the kanji are different. 法 contains the 氵 (water) radical — historically suggesting flowing from a source of justice. 律 contains a component suggesting measured order.
✗ 方立 uses 方 (ほう, direction/method) and 立 (たつ, stand up). 方 also reads ホウ, like 法, causing confusion. But 方立 is not a standard compound meaning law.
✗ 法立 uses the correct 法 (ほう) but replaces 律 with 立 (たつ/リツ). 立 reads リツ in some compounds (e.g., 独立 どくりつ), so the sound is superficially similar. However, 法律 requires 律 (rule), not 立 (stand).
✗ 方律 uses 方 instead of 法. While 方 and 法 both read ホウ, the legal meaning belongs to 法 (which has the 氵 radical). 方律 is not a standard compound.
例: その行為 (こうい) は法律 (ほうりつ) に違反 (いはん) しているので、許 (ゆる) されません。 — That action violates the law and is therefore not permitted.

opts: 方立 – không có từ này (PHƯƠNG LẬP)
法立 – không có từ này (PHÁP LẬP)
方律 – không có từ này (PHƯƠNG LUẬT)
✔ 法律 – ほうりつ, pháp luật (PHÁP LUẬT)
ex.trans: Ở đại học tôi đã học luật.
ex.note: 法 (PHÁP) có bộ nước 氵, 方 (PHƯƠNG) là 'hướng'. 律 (LUẬT) có bộ 彳, đừng nhầm với 立 (đứng).

questions.question: 12 いつか京都をゆっくり ＿かんこう＿ したい。
questions.explanation:
かんこう is written 観光 — 観 (view/observe) + 光 (light/scenery).
観光 (かんこう) means "sightseeing" or "tourism". Both kanji use on-yomi: 観 (カン, to view/observe) + 光 (コウ, light/radiance — here extended to mean the brilliant sights of a place). The sentence 「いつか京都をゆっくりかんこうしたい」 means "Someday I want to take my time sightseeing in Kyoto." The test distinguishes 観 from 歓 (also カン, but meaning "joy/welcome") and 光 from 察 (サツ, investigate). The 見 radical inside 観 signals vision/observation, whereas 歓 contains 欠 (mouth open in joy). Remembering that 観光 is about seeing (観) the scenery (光) helps lock in the correct kanji pair.
✗ 観察 reads かんさつ, not かんこう. 察 (サツ) means "to investigate / to sense", giving 観察 the meaning "observation" (careful watching). The second kanji is wrong.
✗ 歓光 uses 歓 (カン, joy/welcome) instead of 観 (カン, observe). 歓 appears in 歓迎 (かんげい, welcome) and 歓声 (かんせい, cheer). It does not mean watching/viewing scenery.
✗ 歓察 gets both kanji wrong — 歓 instead of 観, and 察 instead of 光. The sounds also fail to match: 歓察 would read かんさつ, not かんこう.
例: 観光 (かんこう) 客 (きゃく) が多 (おお) すぎて、有名 (ゆうめい) な神社 (じんじゃ) に入 (はい) れなかった。 — There were so many tourists that I could not get into the famous shrine.

opts: ✔ 観光 – かんこう, tham quan, du lịch (QUAN QUANG)
観察 – かんさつ 'quan sát', sai nghĩa
歓光 – không có từ này (歓 HOAN = vui)
歓察 – không có từ này
ex.trans: Một ngày nào đó tôi muốn đi tham quan Kyoto thong thả.
ex.note: 観 (QUAN) có bộ 見 bên phải = nhìn; 歓 (HOAN) bộ 欠 = vui mừng (歓迎). 光 (QUANG) = ánh sáng.

questions.question: 13 当日、この ＿けん＿ を忘れないようにしてください。
questions.explanation:
けん (ticket/voucher) is written 券 — the speaker is told not to forget this ticket on the day.
券 (けん) means "a ticket" or "a voucher". The sentence 「当日、このけんを忘れないようにしてください」 means "Please make sure not to forget this ticket on the day of the event." The on-yomi ケン is the standard reading for 券 when it stands alone or at the end of a compound. It appears in: 入場券 (にゅうじょうけん, admission ticket), 乗車券 (じょうしゃけん, train ticket), 商品券 (しょうひんけん, gift voucher). Among the four options, the trap is distinguishing 券 (ticket) from 巻 (roll/volume), 募 (recruit), and 巷 (alleyway) — all of which have partially similar forms.
✗ 巻 reads まき or かん and means "a roll" or "a volume (of a book)". 巻 (まき) is used for sushi rolls, and 巻 (かん) is a counter for book volumes. It does not mean a ticket.
✗ 募 reads ぼ or つの and means "to recruit / to solicit". 募 is used in 応募 (おうぼ, application) and 募集 (ぼしゅう, recruitment). It has no ticket meaning.
✗ 巷 reads こうじ or まち and means "alleyway" or "the town/streets". 巷 is used in set phrases like 巷間 (こうかん, among the public). It has no reading ケン and no ticket meaning.
例: コンサートの入場券 (にゅうじょうけん) は発売開始 (はつばいかいし) から10分 (じゅっぷん) で完売 (かんばい) した。 — Concert tickets sold out within 10 minutes of going on sale.

opts: 巻 – まき/かん, cuộn, tập (QUYỂN)
✔ 券 – けん, vé, phiếu (KHOÁN)
募 – ぼ, tuyển mộ (MỘ)
巷 – ちまた, ngõ phố (HẠNG)
ex.trans: Hôm đó xin đừng quên mang theo vé này.
ex.note: 券 (KHOÁN) dưới là 刀, 巻 (QUYỂN) dưới là 己. Vé = 'dao cắt phiếu' → 刀. 乗車券, 入場券.

questions.question: 14 なかなか ＿なみだ＿ が止まらなくて困りました。
questions.explanation:
なみだ is written 涙 — the kanji for "tears".
涙 (なみだ) means "tears" — the liquid produced when crying. The sentence 「なかなかなみだが止まらなくて困りました」 means "The tears just would not stop, which troubled me." Among the four options, 涙 is the only kanji meaning tears. Its on-yomi is ルイ (as in 感涙 かんるい, tears of emotion), but in everyday speech and in this context the kun-yomi なみだ is always used. The 氵 (water) radical on the left reinforces the liquid nature of tears, and the right component 戻 suggests returning or flowing back — tears flowing from the eyes. This question distinguishes 涙 (なみだ, tears) from three other water-related characters.
✗ 流 reads ながれ or リュウ and means "to flow" or "a current". While tears flow (涙が流れる), 流 itself does not mean "tears" — it describes the action of flowing, not the liquid itself.
✗ 汗 reads あせ and means "sweat". 汗 (あせ) is a different bodily liquid. Sweat and tears are both produced by the body but are distinct — this distractor tests whether learners confuse the two water-radical characters.
✗ 泣 reads なく and means "to cry" — the action of crying, not the tears themselves. 泣く (なく, to cry) and 涙 (なみだ, tears) are conceptually related but 泣 is a verb kanji, not the noun for the liquid.
例: 映画 (えいが) の最後 (さいご) のシーンで涙 (なみだ) が出 (で) てしまった。 — I ended up crying during the last scene of the movie.

opts: 流 – なが(れる), chảy (LƯU)
汗 – あせ, mồ hôi (HÃN)
✔ 涙 – なみだ, nước mắt (LỆ)
泣 – な(く), khóc (KHẤP)
ex.trans: Mãi không cầm được nước mắt nên tôi rất khổ sở.
ex.note: Cả bốn chữ đều bộ nước. 涙 bên phải là 戻; 泣 là động từ 'khóc', 涙 là danh từ 'nước mắt'.

questions.question: 9 やくそくを ＿まもる＿ ことは大切だ。
questions.explanation:
まもる is written 守る because 守る means "to keep / to protect", fitting the importance of keeping a promise.
守る (まもる) = to keep, to protect, to observe (a rule or promise). The sentence says 「やくそくをまもることは大切 (たいせつ) だ」 — "It is important to keep a promise." 約束を守る (やくそくをまもる, to keep a promise) is a set phrase in Japanese. The kanji 守 contains 宀 (roof) on top and 寸 (measurement) below — the image of carefully guarding what is under your roof.
✗ 保る (1 保る): 保 (ほ, to preserve/maintain) is close in meaning to 守 but does not form 保る as a standard conjugated verb. 保つ (たもつ, to maintain) is the correct form for 保 — not 保る.
✗ 2 要 (かなめ/よう): 要 means essential/pivot point, not to keep/protect. 要る (いる, to need) is the verb form of 要. 約束を要る makes no sense in this context.
✗ 4 取る (とる): 取る means to take/get. 約束を取る is not the standard expression for keeping a promise; 約束を守る is. 取 and 守 are different kanji.
例: ルールを守 (まも) ることはチームワークの基本 (きほん) だ。 — Keeping the rules is the basis of teamwork.

opts: 保る – không có cách đọc này (保 BẢO, 保つ たもつ)
要 – よう/い(る), cần (YẾU), không đọc まもる
✔ 守る – まもる, giữ, bảo vệ, tuân thủ (THỦ)
取る – とる, lấy (THỦ)
ex.trans: Giữ lời hứa là điều quan trọng.
ex.note: 守 (THỦ) = mái nhà 宀 + 寸, 'giữ nhà'. 約束を守る, ルールを守る. 取る cũng Hán Việt THỦ nhưng nghĩa 'lấy'.

questions.question: 10 今、この ＿しゅうかんし＿ が一番売れている。
questions.explanation:
しゅうかんし is written 週刊誌 because 刊 means "publication issue" and 誌 means "magazine," giving the compound its precise meaning of "weekly magazine."
週刊誌 (しゅうかんし) means "weekly magazine" — a periodical published once a week. The three kanji each carry a specific meaning: 週 (しゅう) = week, 刊 (かん) = publication issue or print run, 誌 (し) = magazine or periodical. The key kanji to distinguish are the second and third positions. 刊 (かん) is used specifically for published editions: 週刊 (しゅうかん, weekly edition), 月刊 (げっかん, monthly edition), 朝刊 (ちょうかん, morning newspaper). 誌 (し) is used for periodicals and magazines: 雑誌 (ざっし, magazine), 機関誌 (きかんし, organ publication). The word 議 (ぎ, deliberation) in options 1 and 3 is used in words like 会議 (かいぎ, meeting) — it has no connection to publications. The character 間 (かん, interval) in options 1 and 2 is used in 時間 (じかん, time) and 週間 (しゅうかん, a span of one week) — but 週間 refers to duration, not publication type. So 週刊誌 (刊 = print issue + 誌 = magazine) is the only combination that correctly describes a weekly magazine.
✗ 週間議 combines 間 (duration/interval) and 議 (deliberation). 週間 alone means "a period of one week," but 議 is used in meeting-related words like 議論 (ぎろん, debate). This combination describes nothing related to magazines.
✗ 週間誌 uses 間 instead of 刊. While 週間 (しゅうかん) does mean "one week's duration," the standard word for a weekly publication is 週刊 (しゅうかん with 刊, the publication kanji). 週間誌 is not a standard compound.
✗ 週刊議 has the correct 刊 for publication but replaces 誌 with 議 (deliberation). 議 belongs to political and meeting vocabulary (議員 ぎいん, representative; 議会 ぎかい, parliament) and does not mean magazine.
例: この週刊誌 (しゅうかんし) は芸能 (げいのう) ニュースが多い。 — This weekly magazine has a lot of entertainment news.

opts: 週間議 – không có từ này (議 NGHỊ = bàn bạc)
週間誌 – sai: 間 là 'khoảng' (一週間)
週刊議 – không có từ này
✔ 週刊誌 – しゅうかんし, tạp chí tuần (CHU SAN CHÍ)
ex.trans: Bây giờ tạp chí tuần này đang bán chạy nhất.
ex.note: 刊 (SAN) = xuất bản (週刊, 月刊), 間 (GIAN) = khoảng thời gian. 誌 (CHÍ) bộ 言 = tạp chí (雑誌).

questions.question: 11 今日はこれから友達と旅行の ＿そうだん＿ をします。
questions.explanation:
そうだん is written 相談 because 相 means "mutual" and 談 means "to talk/discuss," together meaning "consultation" or "discussing a matter together."
相談 (そうだん) means "consultation," "discussion," or "talking something over with someone." Both kanji take their on-yomi: 相 (そう) = mutual/each other/appearance, and 談 (だん) = to talk/discuss. Together they describe a mutual conversation about a topic — two people talking it through. The sentence says: "Today, from now, I will have a consultation 相談 (そうだん) with a friend about our travel plans." 相談する (そうだんする) is the standard verb for consulting someone or discussing something together. The four options test 相 (そう, mutual) vs 想 (そう, thought/idea) and 談 (だん, to talk) vs 淡 (たん/あわ, pale/light). 相 and 想 both read そう but differ in meaning: 相 is about mutual relationships and appearances, while 想 is about thoughts and imagination (想像 そうぞう, imagination; 感想 かんそう, impression). 談 reads だん (to talk: 会談 かいだん, meeting/talks; 談話 だんわ, conversation), while 淡 reads たん/あわ (pale/light: 淡水 たんすい, freshwater; 淡い あわい, faint).
✗ 想談 uses 想 (そう, thought/imagination) instead of 相 (mutual/appearance). 想談 is not a real compound. 想 belongs in words like 想像 (そうぞう, imagination) and 感想 (かんそう, impressions), not in consultation vocabulary.
✗ 想淡 combines 想 (thought) and 淡 (pale/light) — both wrong. 淡 reads たん/あわ and is used in 淡水 (たんすい, freshwater) and 淡い (あわい, faint/pale). Neither kanji belongs in 相談.
✗ 相淡 uses the correct 相 but replaces 談 with 淡 (pale/light/faint). 談 reads だん and relates to conversation; 淡 reads たん/あわ and relates to lightness or freshness. 相淡 is not a real compound.
例: 進路 (しんろ) について先生 (せんせい) に相談 (そうだん) した。 — I consulted my teacher about my future path.

opts: 想談 – không có từ này (想 TƯỞNG)
想淡 – không có từ này
✔ 相談 – そうだん, bàn bạc, hỏi ý kiến (TƯƠNG ĐÀM)
相淡 – không có từ này (淡 ĐẠM = nhạt)
ex.trans: Hôm nay bây giờ tôi sẽ bàn với bạn về chuyến du lịch.
ex.note: 相 (TƯƠNG) = lẫn nhau; 談 (ĐÀM) bộ 言 = nói chuyện. 淡 bộ nước = nhạt (淡水). 想 có 心 bên dưới.

questions.question: 12 わたしは体力には ＿じしん＿ があります。
questions.explanation:
じしん is written 自信 — 自 (self) + 信 (confidence/belief).
自信 (じしん) means "self-confidence" or "confidence in oneself". Both kanji use on-yomi: 自 (ジ, self) + 信 (シン, belief/trust). Together the word means "trust in oneself". The sentence 「わたしは体力にはじしんがあります」 means "I have confidence in my physical strength." Among the four options, the traps are 持信 (じしん, holding trust — not a standard compound) and 自心 (じしん, not standard). The key distinction is 信 (シン, trust/belief) — seen in 信頼 (しんらい, trust), 信じる (しんじる, to believe) — versus 心 (シン/こころ, heart/mind). Both 信 and 心 share the on-yomi シン, which causes visual and aural confusion.
✗ 持信 uses 持 (ジ/も, hold/have) instead of 自 (ジ, self). While 持 also reads ジ, 持信 is not a fixed compound meaning confidence. 持 is typically kun-yomi もつ in verb uses.
✗ 持心 gets both kanji wrong — 持 instead of 自, and 心 instead of 信. 持心 is not a standard Japanese compound.
✗ 自心 uses 心 (こころ/シン, heart/mind) instead of 信 (シン, belief/trust). Both 信 and 心 read シン, but only 自信 (自 + 信) is the standard compound for self-confidence.
例: 失敗 (しっぱい) を恐 (おそ) れずに挑戦 (ちょうせん) することが自信 (じしん) につながる。 — Attempting challenges without fear of failure leads to self-confidence.

opts: 持信 – không có từ này (持 TRÌ = cầm)
✔ 自信 – じしん, tự tin (TỰ TÍN)
持心 – không có từ này
自心 – không có từ này
ex.trans: Tôi tự tin về thể lực.
ex.note: 自 (TỰ) = bản thân, 信 (TÍN) = tin. 持 (もつ) cũng đọc じ nhưng nghĩa 'cầm, giữ'. Nhớ 自信がある.

questions.question: 13 電子レンジでミルクを ＿あたためました＿ 。
questions.explanation:
あたためました is written 温めました because 温 means "to warm up" something — here, warming milk in a microwave.
温める (あたためる) means "to warm up" or "to heat" — bringing something to a comfortable warm temperature, often food or drink. Its past polite form 温めました (あたためました) describes the completed action. The sentence says: "I warmed milk 温めました (あたためました) in the microwave." 電子レンジでミルクを温める is a completely natural description of a common daily action. The kanji 温 uses the kun-yomi あたた in verb form: 温める (あたためる, transitive: to warm something up), 温まる (あたたまる, intransitive: to warm up by itself). The key distinction among the distractors: 温 (おん/あたた, warm/comfortable warmth — for liquids and food), 熱 (ねつ/あつ, hot/heat — for things that are hot to the touch or fever). Warming milk in a microwave uses 温める (moderate warming), not 熱する (applying intense heat). 湯 (ゆ, hot water) is a noun, not a verb stem. 熟 (じゅく, mature/ripen) is used in 熟す (じゅくす) and 熟れる — it does not mean to warm.
✗ 湯めました uses 湯 (ゆ, hot water). 湯 is a noun meaning hot water or hot spring water. It does not function as a verb meaning to warm something up. 湯める is not a standard verb form.
✗ 熟めました uses 熟 (じゅく), meaning to ripen or mature — as in 熟す (じゅくす, to ripen). Ripening fruit and warming milk are different processes. 熟 does not read あたため.
✗ 熱めました uses 熱 (ねつ/あつ), meaning hot heat or fever. 熱する (ねっする) means to apply high heat, 熱い (あつい) means hot to the touch. Warming milk gently in a microwave is 温める (mild warmth), not 熱する (intense heat). 熱 does not read あたためました.
例: 寒 (さむ) い日 (ひ) は温 (あたた) かいスープを温 (あたた) めて飲 (の) むと体 (からだ) が楽 (らく) になる。 — On cold days, warming up some soup and drinking it makes the body feel better.

opts: ✔ 温めました – あたためました, hâm nóng (ÔN)
湯めました – không có cách đọc này (湯 THANG = nước nóng)
熟めました – không có (熟 THỤC = chín)
熱めました – không có (熱 NHIỆT, 熱い あつい)
ex.trans: Tôi đã hâm nóng sữa bằng lò vi sóng.
ex.note: 温める (あたためる) và 暖める đều đọc あたためる; 温 cho đồ ăn/nước, 暖 cho phòng/không khí. 熱 là tính từ 熱い.

questions.question: 14 この製品の ＿げんりょう＿ はすべて輸入しています。
questions.explanation:
げんりょう is written 原料 because 原 means "original/raw" and 料 means "material/fee," together meaning "raw materials."
原料 (げんりょう) means "raw materials" or "ingredients" — the base substances used to manufacture a product. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 原 (げん) = original/raw/source, and 料 (りょう) = material/fee. Together they describe original source materials. The sentence says: "All raw materials 原料 (げんりょう) for this product are imported." 原料はすべて輸入している = "all raw materials are imported" is common in manufacturing contexts. The key distinction is between 原 (げん, original/raw source) and 材 (ざい, timber/material). 材料 (ざいりょう) and 原料 (げんりょう) are near-synonyms, but: 原料 (げんりょう) = raw materials before any processing, the fundamental inputs; 材料 (ざいりょう) = materials or ingredients more broadly, including partially processed materials. The second distinction: 料 (りょう, material/fee) vs 量 (りょう, quantity/amount). Same sound, different meaning and kanji. 量 appears in 分量 (ぶんりょう, portion) and 重量 (じゅうりょう, weight).
✗ 材料 (ざいりょう) is a real word meaning "material(s)" or "ingredients." It uses 材 (ざい, timber/material) instead of 原 (げん, raw source). While related, 材料 is used for cooking ingredients and construction materials, while 原料 specifically refers to unprocessed raw inputs. Also, 材料 reads ざいりょう (不 げんりょう), so this option is wrong both in kanji and reading.
✗ 材量 uses 材 (material) for the first kanji and 量 (quantity) for the second. 量 reads りょう but means "quantity" — not material/fee. 材量 is not a standard compound.
✗ 原量 has the correct first kanji 原 (げん) but uses 量 (quantity) instead of 料 (material). 量 means amount or quantity (重量 じゅうりょう, 分量 ぶんりょう), not raw substance. 原量 is not a standard compound.
例: この食品 (しょくひん) の原料 (げんりょう) はすべて国内 (こくない) で栽培 (さいばい) されたものだ。 — All the raw materials for this food product are grown domestically.

opts: 材料 – ざいりょう 'vật liệu, nguyên liệu nấu ăn', đọc khác
材量 – không có từ này
✔ 原料 – げんりょう, nguyên liệu thô (NGUYÊN LIỆU)
原量 – không có từ này
ex.trans: Nguyên liệu của sản phẩm này đều nhập khẩu.
ex.note: 料 (LIỆU) = vật liệu, 量 (LƯỢNG) = số lượng. 原料 là nguyên liệu thô để sản xuất; 材料 là vật liệu/nguyên liệu nấu.

questions.question: 13 リボンをきれいに ＿むすぶ＿ のは難しい。
questions.explanation:
むすぶ is written 結ぶ because 結 means "to tie / to connect," which is what you do when you tie a ribbon.
結ぶ (むすぶ) means "to tie," "to knot," or "to connect." The kanji 結 has the on-yomi けつ (as in 結果 けっか, result; 結婚 けっこん, marriage) and the kun-yomi むすぶ. In verb form, 結ぶ always uses the kun-yomi むすぶ. The sentence says: "It is difficult to tie a ribbon 結ぶ (むすぶ) neatly." Tying something — especially something decorative like a ribbon — is precisely what 結ぶ means. The radical of 結 is 糸 (いと, thread/fiber), which is a strong hint: anything involving tying, knotting, or connecting threads falls under kanji with the 糸 radical. The distractors 組, 洛, and 給 all contain different radicals and mean completely different things. When you see the action of tying or knotting in a sentence, 結ぶ is the standard word.
✗ 組 (くむ/そ) means "to assemble," "to combine," or "a group/set." 腕を組む (うでをくむ) means "to fold one's arms." It does not mean to tie a ribbon — that action requires 結ぶ.
✗ 洛 is a kanji primarily used in place names (like 洛陽 らくよう, Luoyang in China, or an old name for Kyoto). It has no reading むすぶ and no meaning related to tying. This is a visually distracting option with no semantic connection.
✗ 給 (きゅう) means "to supply" or "salary" — as in 給料 (きゅうりょう, salary) and 給食 (きゅうしょく, school lunch). It does not read むすぶ and has no meaning of tying or connecting.
例: プレゼントに赤いリボンを結 (むす) んだ。 — I tied a red ribbon on the present.

opts: 組ぶ – không có (組 TỔ, 組む くむ)
洛ぶ – không có từ này (洛 LẠC)
給ぶ – không có (給 CẤP)
✔ 結ぶ – むすぶ, buộc, thắt (KẾT)
ex.trans: Thắt nơ cho đẹp là việc khó.
ex.note: 結 (KẾT) bộ chỉ 糸 + 吉 = buộc dây. 結ぶ (buộc), 結果 (kết quả), 結婚 (kết hôn). 組む là 'đan, khoanh'.

questions.question: 100 年後の世界を ＿想像＿ するのは難しい。
questions.explanation:
想像 is read そうぞう and means "to imagine" — picturing what the world will look like 100 years from now.
想像 (そうぞう) is an on-yomi compound: 想 (ソウ, think/imagine) + 像 (ゾウ, image/figure). Together the word means "imagination" or "to picture mentally". The sentence 「100年後の世界を想像するのは難しい」 means "It is difficult to imagine what the world will be like 100 years from now." Both characters use their on-yomi. A key phonological feature here is the voiced 濁音 (だくおん): 像 reads ゾウ — voiced — rather than ソウ. This voicing is a common N3 reading trap. Compare the distractor そぞう, which drops the long vowel from 想 (ソウ), and そうしょう, which replaces 像 (ゾウ) with the wrong reading シュウ.
✗ そぞう drops the long vowel in 想 — the correct on-yomi is ソウ (long vowel), not ソ. Shortening the first vowel produces a non-word.
✗ そしょう misreads 像 as ショウ. 像 reads ゾウ, not ショウ. ショウ belongs to other kanji in different contexts, but 想像 uses ゾウ for 像.
✗ そうしょう also misreads 像 as ショウ, and adds a small tsu before it, producing a sound that does not match any reading of this compound.
例: その小説 (しょうせつ) は想像力 (そうぞうりょく) をとても豊 (ゆた) かにしてくれる。 — That novel greatly enriches one's imagination.

opts: そぞう – thiếu trường âm, sai
そしょう – 訴訟 'kiện tụng', không phải chữ này
✔ そうぞう – 想像, tưởng tượng (TƯỞNG TƯỢNG)
そうしょう – không có từ này
ex.trans: Thật khó tưởng tượng thế giới 100 năm sau.
ex.note: TƯỞNG TƯỢNG. Cả hai âm dài: そう・ぞう. Đồng âm với 創造 (sáng tạo) cũng đọc そうぞう.

questions.question: ＿やっきよく＿ がなかなか見つかりません。
questions.explanation:
やっきよく is written 薬局 — 薬 (medicine/drug) + 局 (bureau/office/pharmacy).
薬局 (やっきょく) means "a pharmacy" or "a drugstore". Both kanji use on-yomi: 薬 (ヤク→やっ with gemination before a consonant) + 局 (キョク). Together the word literally means "a medicine office" — the place where drugs are dispensed. The sentence 「やっきよくがなかなか見つかりません」 means "I cannot find a pharmacy easily." The phonological feature here is the gemination: 薬 reads ヤク, and when followed by the consonant-initial キョク, ヤク → やっ (promoting the final ク to っ). This gives やっ + きょく = やっきょく. Among the four options, 薬局 is the only compound using the correct characters: 薬 (medicine) + 局 (bureau).
✗ 薬曲 uses 曲 (きょく, music/curve) instead of 局 (きょく, bureau/office). Both 曲 and 局 share the on-yomi キョク, which causes the confusion. 薬曲 is not a standard compound.
✗ 楽局 uses 楽 (がく/ラク, music/enjoyment) instead of 薬 (ヤク, medicine). 楽 and 薬 look similar — 薬 has 艹 (grass) on top while 楽 does not. 楽局 is not a standard compound.
✗ 楽曲 reads がっきょく and means "a musical piece" or "a composition". It gets both kanji wrong — 楽 instead of 薬, and 曲 instead of 局. 楽曲 is a real word but has nothing to do with pharmacies.
例: 処方箋 (しょほうせん) を持 (も) って近 (ちか) くの薬局 (やっきょく) で薬 (くすり) をもらった。 — I took my prescription to the nearby pharmacy and received the medicine.

opts: ✔ 薬局 – やっきょく, hiệu thuốc (DƯỢC CỤC)
薬曲 – không có từ này (曲 KHÚC = bài hát)
楽局 – không có từ này
楽曲 – がっきょく 'bản nhạc', đọc khác
ex.trans: Tôi mãi không tìm thấy hiệu thuốc.
ex.note: 薬 (DƯỢC) = 艹 + 楽; 楽 (NHẠC) không có 艹. 局 (CỤC) = cơ quan (郵便局, 薬局); 曲 (KHÚC) = bài hát. Đọc やっきょく (rút âm).

questions.question: 「生」の読み方で「なま」の場合、意味はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
生 read as なま means 'raw' or 'fresh' — uncooked and unprocessed.
生 (なま) is a unique kanji with multiple readings. The kun-yomi なま means 'raw,' 'fresh,' or 'unprocessed' — appearing in 生魚 (なまざかな, raw fish), 生卵 (なまたまご, raw egg), 生ビール (なまビール, draft beer), and 生放送 (なまほうそう, live broadcast). The key idea is that nothing has been applied to the thing — no cooking, no processing, no intermediary. 生 also has other readings: いき (lively), せい (on-yomi, as in 先生 せんせい), しょう (on-yomi), and はえる (to grow). At N3 level, distinguishing these readings by context is essential.
✗ Cooked is the direct opposite of なま. Cooking applies heat and changes the fundamental state of food.
✗ Frozen food is 冷凍 (れいとう) — processed by cold storage. 生 (なま) means untreated and unprocessed, independent of temperature.
✗ Dried (乾燥した かんそうした) means moisture has been removed — a form of processing. This is the opposite of なま's unprocessed state.
例: この魚 (さかな) は生 (なま) で食 (た) べられます。 — This fish can be eaten raw.

opts: cooked – đã nấu chín, ngược nghĩa
frozen – đông lạnh
dried – sấy khô
✔ raw/fresh – sống, tươi (生 なま)
ex.trans: Khi 生 đọc là なま thì nghĩa là gì? → sống, tươi.
ex.note: 生 SINH có nhiều cách đọc: なま (sống: 生ビール), いきる (sống), うまれる (sinh ra), せい (学生).

questions.question: 「がっかり」の意味はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
がっかり means 'disappointed' — the deflated feeling when expectations are not met.
がっかり is an adverb and する-verb (がっかりする) meaning 'to be disappointed' or 'to feel let down.' It describes the specific emotion of having had an expectation or hope that did not come true. 試験 (しけん) に落 (お) ちてがっかりした (I was disappointed to fail the exam), 雨 (あめ) でピクニックが中止 (ちゅうし) になってがっかりした (I was disappointed when the picnic was cancelled due to rain). The word carries a deflated, downcast quality — the energy you had drops away. がっかりさせる means 'to disappoint (someone),' and がっかりするな means 'don't be disappointed.' This is a high-frequency N3 vocabulary item that appears in dialogues and short passages.
✗ 'excited' is わくわくする or 興奮 (こうふん) する. Excitement is the energized buildup of expectation; がっかり is the deflated result when that expectation fails.
✗ 'surprised' is びっくりする or 驚く (おどろく). Surprise is a sudden reaction to the unexpected; がっかり is about an expected positive outcome that did not occur.
✗ 'relieved' is ほっとする or 安心 (あんしん) する. Relief happens when a feared negative outcome does NOT occur; がっかり happens when a hoped positive outcome does NOT occur. They are on opposite sides of the emotion spectrum.
例: 楽 (たの) しみにしていたコンサートが中止 (ちゅうし) になってがっかりした。 — I was disappointed when the concert I had been looking forward to was cancelled.

opts: excited – hào hứng
surprised – ngạc nhiên
relieved – nhẹ nhõm
✔ disappointed – thất vọng (がっかり)
ex.trans: がっかり nghĩa là gì? → thất vọng.
ex.note: がっかりする = thất vọng, hụt hẫng vì kỳ vọng không thành. Thường đi với 試験に落ちて, 負けて.

questions.question: 「文字」の読み方はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
文字 is read もじ and means 'letter / character / written symbol.'
文字 (もじ) is a common compound meaning 'a character,' 'a letter,' or 'a written symbol.' It refers to any individual unit of writing: kanji, hiragana, a Roman letter, a numeral. 文 (もん → も) uses a special rendaku-influenced kun-yomi in this compound — the usual on-yomi is ぶん or もん, but in the word 文字, it reads も. 字 (じ) means 'character / letter,' and in compounds its on-yomi is じ. So 文字 = も＋じ = もじ. This reading is irregular and must be memorized. 文字 appears in everyday contexts: 文字化け (もじばけ, garbled text), 漢字 (かんじ) は表意文字 (ひょういもじ) だ (kanji are ideographic characters). A related word is 字 (じ) alone, which can informally mean 'handwriting': 字が上手 (うま) い (your handwriting is good).
✗ もんじ applies the on-yomi もん to 文 and じ to 字. もん is one standard reading for 文 (as in 文句, もんく, complaint), but 文字 uses the special compound reading もじ, not もんじ. These two sounds are close but distinct.
✗ ぶんし applies the formal on-yomi ぶん to 文 and し to 字. ぶん is used in 文章 (ぶんしょう, sentence) or 文化 (ぶんか, culture), but not in 文字. And 字 reads じ, not し.
✗ ぶんじ uses ぶん for 文 and じ for 字. The second half is correct (じ), but ぶん is the wrong reading for 文 in this compound. もじ is the set reading for 文字.
例: スマートフォンの画面 (がめん) の文字 (もじ) が小 (ちい) さすぎて読 (よ) めない。 — The text on the smartphone screen is too small to read.

opts: もんじ – cách đọc cũ của 文字, ít dùng
✔ もじ – 文字, chữ, ký tự (VĂN TỰ)
ぶんし – 分子 'phân tử', không phải chữ này
ぶんじ – không có từ này
ex.trans: 文字 đọc là gì? → もじ (chữ viết).
ex.note: 文 VĂN ở đây đọc も (không phải ぶん), 字 TỰ → じ. Nhớ 絵文字 えもじ, 大文字 おおもじ.

questions.question: 「人類」の読み方はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
人類 is read じんるい and means 'humanity' or 'humankind' — all human beings as a species.
人類 (じんるい) means humankind, humanity, or the human species as a whole. 人 (じん) has the on-yomi じん and means 'person' or 'human'; it appears in 人間 (にんげん, human being) and 外国人 (がいこくじん, foreigner). 類 (るい) has the on-yomi るい and means 'type,' 'category,' or 'species'; it appears in 種類 (しゅるい, type/variety) and 類似 (るいじ, resemblance). Together: じんるい = 'the human species/category' = humankind. Common uses: 人類の歴史 (じんるいのれきし, human history), 人類共通の問題 (じんるいきょうつうのもんだい, problems common to all humanity). Note: 人 uses the on-yomi じん (not にん) in this compound because じん is more common when preceding るい.
✗ じんたぐい applies the on-yomi じん to 人 and a non-standard たぐい reading to 類 (たぐい is a kun-yomi of 類 meaning 'the like of'). In the compound 人類, 類 uses the on-yomi るい.
✗ ひとるい applies the kun-yomi ひと of 人 and the on-yomi るい of 類. Half right, but 人 uses its on-yomi じん in this compound.
✗ にんるい applies the on-yomi にん to 人 and the correct on-yomi るい to 類. While にん is a valid on-yomi of 人 (as in 人間 (にんげん) or 人形 (にんぎょう)), in 人類, the more natural reading is じんるい.
例: 環境問題 (かんきょうもんだい) は人類 (じんるい) 全体 (ぜんたい) で取 (と) り組 (く) むべき課題 (かだい) だ。 — Environmental issues are challenges that all of humankind must address together.

opts: じんたぐい – không có từ này
ひとるい – không có từ này
にんるい – không có từ này
✔ じんるい – 人類, nhân loại, loài người (NHÂN LOẠI)
ex.trans: 人類 đọc là gì? → じんるい (nhân loại).
ex.note: 人 đọc じん trong từ Hán trang trọng (人類, 人生 じんせい), にん trong 人間 にんげん, 人気 にんき.

questions.question: 「休憩」の読み方はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
休憩 is read きゅうけい and means 'a short break' from work or activity.
休憩 (きゅうけい) is an on-yomi compound. 休 (きゅう) means 'to rest / to pause,' and 憩 (けい) means 'to rest temporarily / to take a breath.' Together they describe a brief, intentional pause from activity — a coffee break, a lunch break, a five-minute rest during a long task. 休憩する means 'to take a break.' Common contexts: 休憩時間 (きゅうけいじかん, break time), 一時間後に休憩しましょう (let's take a break in an hour). The reading きゅうけい uses on-yomi for both characters. 休 (きゅう) appears widely: 休日 (きゅうじつ, holiday), 夏休み (なつやすみ, summer break). 憩 (けい) is a less common character that appears almost exclusively in 休憩 and 憩いの場 (いこいのば, a place of rest).
✗ やすかい assigns the kun-yomi やす from 休む (やすむ) to 休 and kaい to 憩. 憩 does not have a standard reading kaい. The on-yomi of the compound is きゅう, not やす.
✗ やすけい also uses the kun-yomi やす for 休 (incorrect in a compound) but correctly reads 憩 as けい. Half-correct readings are still wrong.
✗ きゅうかい correctly reads 休 as きゅう but assigns かい to 憩. かい is the on-yomi for characters like 解 (かい, solve) or 海 (かい, sea). 憩 reads けい, not かい.
例: 長時間 (ちょうじかん) の会議 (かいぎ) の途中 (とちゅう) で休憩 (きゅうけい) を取 (と) った。 — We took a break in the middle of the long meeting.

opts: ✔ きゅうけい – 休憩, nghỉ giải lao (HƯU KHẾ)
やすかい – không có từ này
やすけい – không có từ này
きゅうかい – không có từ này
ex.trans: 休憩 đọc là gì? → きゅうけい (nghỉ giải lao).
ex.note: 憩 KHẾ → けい. 休憩時間 きゅうけいじかん = giờ nghỉ giải lao. Phân biệt với 休暇 きゅうか.

questions.question: 「休暇」の読み方はなんですか。
questions.explanation:
休暇 is read きゅうか and means 'vacation / holiday leave.'
休暇 (きゅうか) is a formal word for time off from work or school — vacation, leave, or holiday. 休 (きゅう) means 'rest / pause,' and 暇 (か) means 'free time / leisure.' The compound きゅうか has a formal, official feel. You typically see it in workplace and administrative contexts: 有給休暇 (ゆうきゅうきゅうか, paid vacation), 夏季休暇 (かききゅうか, summer holiday), 産前休暇 (さんぜんきゅうか, maternity leave). The everyday, casual word for vacation is 休み (やすみ), but 休暇 signals a formal entitlement or scheduled period of leave. On the JLPT, 休暇 frequently appears in work-related reading passages.
✗ きゅうけ replaces the correct final vowel. 暇 reads か, not け. The え-sound is not a reading for 暇 in any compound.
✗ やすけ uses the kun-yomi of 休 (やす, as in 休む) and adds an invented け ending. Even if using kun-yomi, 休 reads やすみ, and 暇 still does not read け.
✗ やすか correctly identifies the か ending for 暇 but uses the wrong on/kun pairing. 休 in this word uses on-yomi きゅう, not kun-yomi やす.
例: 来週 (らいしゅう) から夏季休暇 (かききゅうか) に入 (はい) ります。 — I will be on summer vacation starting next week.

opts: ✔ きゅうか – 休暇, kỳ nghỉ, ngày nghỉ phép (HƯU HẠ)
